collection: third-party published SharpHound collection, not our own lab

supersedes.why_it_changed: Schema change only, no re-collection. SpoofSIDHistory was unknown to ad_schema when this was frozen, so its 2 cross-forest edges were dropped; it is now categorised and weighted, so they load. Anything citing this hash is looking at a graph that cannot express the cross-forest move.

Line endings only - the graph content is byte-for-byte equivalent. This hash was not reproducible: AttackGraph.save() wrote platform-default line endings, so freezing the same collection on Linux would have produced a different hash, and core.autocrlf meant the blob git stored differed from the file on disk. save() now writes LF explicitly and .gitattributes marks data/*.json as -text. No re-collection, no re-ingest, no schema change; node/edge counts, provenance and all routes are identical.

ingested_with: BloodHound CE (docker compose, neo4j 4.4.42), post-processing applied
why_not_our_own_lab: GOAD deployment was blocked on a hypervisor conflict (VBS/Memory Integrity + WSL2 + Docker Desktop held VT-x, and VirtualBox 7.2.4 exceeds GOAD's documented <=7.1.x ceiling). Using a published GOADv2 collection keeps real SharpHound schema and real edge semantics while skipping the lab build.

structural_absences_pattern.note: TWO structural absences in this one collection, not one. Sessions are near-absent and delegation is entirely absent. Stating them together because the pattern matters more than either alone: a published lab collection captures whatever that lab happened to have configured and running at that moment, and GOADv2 had neither realistic session activity nor any delegation. A collection from a different lab would have different holes, not fewer. Any claim about coverage of the risk model against real data has to name both.
structural_absences_pattern.delegation: ZERO AllowedToDelegate / AllowedToAct / AddAllowedToAct edges. Not dropped - they do not exist. msds-allowedtodelegateto is empty on every node; only the three DCs have unconstrained delegation, which these edge types do not model. The three delegation weights are sourced but UNEXERCISED BY REAL DATA: nothing in this graph traverses them, so no route or cost here depends on them.
structural_absences_pattern.delegation_but_synthetic_does_use_it: IMPORTANT: synthetic.random_ad() DOES generate AllowedToDelegate edges (24 across 12 seeds). So that weight feeds any statistic computed over generated graphs even though the real collection never exercises it. AllowedToAct and AddAllowedToAct are generated by nothing and are exercised by neither. Do not let a number derived from random_ad be described as grounded in real data.
structural_absences_pattern.sessions_see_below: The session gap is detailed in the next block.

sessions.note: Reflects an idle, freshly-deployed lab rather than live usage: nobody had logged in and left credentials in memory when this was collected. HasSession is a whole risk category (credential theft from a live session) and one of the two main routes in the synthetic fixture, so this graph under-represents that class of attack. Not fixable here - the runbook's remedy is 'log a few users in and re-collect', which needs a lab we control.

adcs_deferred.note: AD CS is present in this collection (2 EnterpriseCA, 2 RootCA, 2 AIACA, 2 NTAuthStore, 71 CertTemplate) and its edges were dropped at load rather than categorised. Certificate-abuse paths are therefore absent from this graph. Deliberate deferral, see docs/stage2_joint_capability_audit.md.
adcs_deferred.consequence: Any route that would have run through certificate abuse is missing, so path costs here are an upper bound on what a real attacker would pay.

other_dropped_types.note: ADCS was not the only thing dropped. See dropped_unknown_edge_types (recorded automatically by the loader) for the full list.
other_dropped_types.AllExtendedRights: 88 edges. Confirmed Shape E - target-kind-dependent, behaving as DCSync-equivalent against a Domain, ForceChangePassword-equivalent against a User, ReadLAPSPassword-equivalent against a LAPS computer. Dropped pending the kind-aware costing work rather than flattened to one number. Do NOT model it as granting RBCD; BloodHound's own historical docs made that link and it is wrong.
other_dropped_types.ClaimSpecialIdentity: 25 edges. Checked, not assumed: the special-identity groups hold zero outbound rights and every edge terminates in another special-identity pseudo-group, so the cluster is a dead end. Dropped because it adds nothing, not because it is unsafe.
other_dropped_types.DCFor: 3 edges. Redundant with the isdc computer property, which is present and agrees exactly. Left dropped; DC targeting, if adopted, can key on isdc without needing this edge.
other_dropped_types.resolved_since: CrossForestTrust / SameForestTrust are no longer dropped - TrustedBy was retired from the schema and these two admitted as structural. MemberOfLocalGroup / LocalToComputer likewise admitted as structural.

traversal_notes.gpo_expansion_required: This graph's only unprivileged attack paths run through the GPO chain. Under the default traversal set just 53 of 783 nodes reach a tier-0 target and the 23 users among them are almost all already privileged. AttackGraph.with_gpo_expansion() lifts that to 70 and is what gives SAMWELL.TARLY a route. Plan over that view, not the raw graph.
traversal_notes.trusts_are_structural: Cross-domain movement here does NOT run over the trusts. It runs over ordinary cross-domain ACLs - GenericAll (71), WriteDacl (19), WriteOwner (19), GenericWrite (18), MemberOf (12), AddKeyCredentialLink (12), AdminTo (1). The trust edges record that a trust exists; crossing a forest boundary as an attacker needs SpoofSIDHistory, which is not yet weighted.
traversal_notes.local_admin_chain_is_gated: MemberOfLocalGroup / LocalToComputer are walkable only via with_local_admin_expansion(), which admits the chain solely out of privileged local groups (RID 544, 555). Ungated, membership in local Users would reach every DC.

entry_points.note: Nothing in this collection is marked owned, so entry nodes are named explicitly rather than inferred. All three below have verified routes to a tier-0 target.
entry_points.SAMWELL.TARLY@NORTH.SEVENKINGDOMS.LOCAL: 2 hops, WriteOwner -> GPLink -> NORTH domain. GPO abuse. Requires with_gpo_expansion().
entry_points.SQL_SVC@NORTH.SEVENKINGDOMS.LOCAL: 4 hops, SQLAdmin -> HasSession -> AdminTo -> DCSync -> NORTH domain. One of the few routes exercising the surviving session data.
entry_points.TYWIN.LANNISTER@SEVENKINGDOMS.LOCAL: 9 hops, ForceChangePassword -> GenericWrite -> WriteDacl -> AddSelf -> AddMember -> WriteOwner -> GenericAll -> GenericAll -> DCSync. Five distinct technique categories - the most useful route for telling a risk-aware planner apart from shortest-path.
entry_points.ESSOS.LOCAL: NO unprivileged entry point exists. Checked, not overlooked: no enabled non-admin user in ESSOS reaches any tier-0 target. Its paths run through the dropped ADCS edges or the unweighted SpoofSIDHistory trust. This is a real and correct characteristic of the graph as it currently stands, not a collection gap to be worked around - do not manufacture an ESSOS entry point.

provenance_caveat: We did not collect this. It cannot be re-collected, varied, or corrected. Every number derived from this graph inherits whatever this snapshot happens to contain.

raw_collection.why_vendored: The frozen graph's ground truth is BloodHound CE's own ingest of these exact files. The parser is validated by reproducing that ingest, so if the upstream repository disappears the validation property disappears with it. 96 KB, Unlicense, so vendoring is cheap and the check stays runnable offline like every other test.
raw_collection.why_refused: The same upstream repository also holds ce_branch_bloodhoundpy_* exports collected 2024-04-11 by bloodhound.py, not by SharpHound 2.3.3. They describe the same lab but are a different collection from a different collector, and they did not produce 3c1bef97. Validating against them would compare our parser to the wrong ingest and still look green, so the loader refuses them by name rather than warning about them.
